item.title: Nadroga bracing for another epic battle with Malolo
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/09/2026 The Nadroga Rugby side will be looking to avenge their 26-24 loss to Malolo in last year’s Skipper Cup season when the two teams meet at Lawaqa Park this afternoon in Round 7.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/09/2026

The Nadroga Rugby side will be looking to avenge their 26-24 loss to Malolo in last year’s Skipper Cup season when the two teams meet at Lawaqa Park this afternoon in Round 7.

Malolo raced to a 20-7 lead at halftime before Nadroga fought their way back into the contest, setting up a tense finish.

With just one point separating the two sides on the competition table, the encounter shapes up as one of the key matches of the weekend as the race for the knockout stages intensifies.

Nadroga have won four of their six matches this season, with one loss and one draw, while Malolo have five wins and one loss.

In other matches, Nadi will take on Ba at King Charles Park, Kadavu will meet Tailevu at Burebasaga School Ground, Taveuni will host Rewa at Wairiki School Ground, and Naitasiri will meet Navosa at Ratu Cakobau Park.

item.title: Ba carries community pride into BOG semi-final against Suva
item.description: The Men in Black are one win away from another final, with Dayal's Steel Ba FC President Praneel Dayal calling on the side to give everything for the badge in today’s Extra Battle of the Giants semi-final. Dayal says while Ba has already won two trophies this season, the team is not taking its success for granted.
item.content:encoded:
The Men in Black are one win away from another final, with Dayal's Steel Ba FC President Praneel Dayal calling on the side to give everything for the badge in today’s Extra Battle of the Giants semi-final.

Dayal says while Ba has already won two trophies this season, the team is not taking its success for granted.

He says success is earned through hard work, humility and staying loyal to your roots.

He says the Ba badge is more than just a badge, as it represents the community, its history and its pride.

Dayal says when the players take the field in the black jersey today, they will carry the pride of Ba and its supporters with them.

He is also calling on Ba fans to come out in numbers and get behind the Men in Black as they fight for a place in the BOG final.

Ba will face Global Care Suva FC at 2pm today at 4R Stadium, Govind Park, in Ba.

Meanwhile, Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC will take on Nasinu FC at 4.30pm in the second semi-final.

The BOG final will kick off at 3pm tomorrow.

item.title: Suva held to 17-all draw by Lautoka
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/09/2026 Suva drew 17-all with Lautoka in their Round 7 Skipper Cup clash held at Bidesi Park.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/09/2026

Suva drew 17-all with Lautoka in their Round 7 Skipper Cup clash held at Bidesi Park.

Lautoka, who sits in 11th place on the points table, led Suva 10-5 at halftime.

Suva managed to regroup in the second half, piling on another 12 points. However, the Sugar City side broke through the capital side’s defence, scoring a try to level the scores at full time.

Meanwhile, Suva beat Lautoka 52-24 in the Subrails Marama Championship and 50-21 in the U20 competition.

In other matches today, Malolo will face Nadroga at Lawaqa Park, Nadi will take on Ba at King Charles Park, Kadavu will meet Tailevu at Burebasaga School Ground, Taveuni will host Rewa at Wairiki School Ground, and Naitasiri will meet Navosa at Ratu Cakobau Park.

item.title: Knights march into week two with 20-10 win over Rabbitohs
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/09/2026 The Newcastle Knights will march on to week two of the finals after a convincing 20-10 win over the Rabbitohs at Allianz Stadium last night.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/09/2026

The Newcastle Knights will march on to week two of the finals after a convincing 20-10 win over the Rabbitohs at Allianz Stadium last night.

A double to Jermaine McEwen and 285 run metres from Kalyn Ponga laid the platform for the Knights’ first finals victory away from home since 2013.

The loss of Cody Walker to a calf injury in the first half left the Bunnies short of ideas in attack, while Jayden Sullivan couldn’t get his kicking game in order in the second half.

The Newcastle Knights will march on to week two, where they will face the loser of the Warriors-Dolphins clash.

In today’s matches, the Warriors will face the Dolphins at 6.05pm, while the Sharks will meet the Cowboys at 9.50pm.

item.content:encoded:
As the FIJI Water Flying Fijians continue their preparations for their Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup clash against Canada tomorrow, Acting Head Coach Senirusi Seruvakula is confident the young team will deliver for the nation.

Seruvakula has named a formidable 23-member squad, including four debutants — Kadavu rugby player and former national men’s 7s rep Terio Tamani, Taveuni rugby player Inoke Ravuiwasa, and Nadroga’s Penaia Cakobau and Isoa Tuwai.

Seruvakula says all the players are in good health, with no injuries in camp.

He says, as defending champions, they are wary of a strong Canadian side that has improved over the past few seasons.

Insert: Seruvakula on debutants, 11th Sep

Fiji will face Canada tomorrow at 7pm Fiji time in Japan.

item.title: Seaqaqa faces Tavua in crucial Premier Division promotion clash
item.description: Seaqaqa are hoping to make history tomorrow as they chase promotion to the Premier Division. They will face Tavua in the promotion-relegation decider before the Extra Battle of the Giants Grand Final.
item.content:encoded:
Seaqaqa are hoping to make history tomorrow as they chase promotion to the Premier Division.

They will face Tavua in the promotion-relegation decider before the Extra Battle of the Giants Grand Final.

After nearly a decade of trying, Seaqaqa say this could finally be their chance to earn promotion and join Labasa in the Premier Division.

Team patron and businessman Mohammed Aruf Khan says the team has worked hard for the past ten years to reach this stage, and there is strong belief within the camp that they can achieve their goal tomorrow.

Khan says coach Imran Khan, who is also a teacher at Salove Primary School, has worked tirelessly with the players in preparing the team.

Seaqaqa and Tavua met last week, with Seaqaqa taking a 1-0 lead before Tavua found an equaliser in the dying stages of the match.

Khan says tomorrow's encounter will be tough and crucial, particularly with a big crowd expected.

He acknowledges Tavua's strength and experience, having previously competed in the Premier Division.

Khan is now calling on Seaqaqa supporters to turn up in numbers and get behind the team as they chase a historic promotion.

The promotion-relegation match between Seaqaqa and Tavua will kick off at 11.30am tomorrow at 4R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba.

Meanwhile, the BOG semi-finals will see Ba take on Suva at 2pm, while Rewa will face Nasinu at 4.30pm today.
